resolved: The historical recording event is dated and identified as G&T Paris 2 May 1903; independent Marston discography fixes Bridal Procession as matrix 2151F / catalog 35517 while Mattes documents why matrix identity is the relevant control across copies.

The selected direct object is deliberately the later Chasing the Butterfly web-access derivative, not a claim that History Go possesses the 1903 master: the HTTPS project page and embedded filename-level Bridal Procession locator are stable and inspectable.

The missing exact physical-copy/checksum/transfer lineage behind the web excerpt is documented as a known source-critical boundary; the released claim does not depend on resolving it and explicitly forbids unmediated-sonic or exact-original-pitch inference.
Rights are resolved for History Go use conservatively: the website states ©2010 and no reuse license is identified, therefore only external-link-and-metadata access is released.
direct_object_gate.release_rule: Only the source-critical distinction between controlled 1903 recording identity and later transfer/restoration/web-access layers may drive a question. Preserve the incomplete source-copy-to-web-file chain, block unmediated-sonic/intention claims, and keep all derivative audio external-link-and-metadata-only.

coverage.known_gap: This production verifies one recording-provenance case. It does not establish the exact surviving shellac source used for the Chasing web excerpt, a complete master-to-file checksum chain, exact original studio pitch, representativeness of Grieg's recorded performance practice, or broader archive-source criticism beyond this object.
